Chile Trample Romania at Junior Challenger

Discover more
Buy Maps
rugby team
Rugby

Americas Rugby News October 7, 2026 Chile, Others, Romania 0 Comments 179 Views

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:00
Instaread

Chile demonstrated progress today with a dominant 50–9 victory against Romania at u20 level. The result highlighted a masterful performance by the host nation in Round 2 of the 2026 World Rugby Under 20 Challenger Cup.

Playing on their home turf at the Centro de Alto Rendimiento de Rugby (CARR) in Santiago, the young Chilean squad, affectionately known as Los Cóndores M20, dictated the pace of the game from the opening whistle. Their relentless attacking pressure and disciplined defense completely overwhelmed the Romanian side, turning what was expected to be a tightly contested physical battle into a lopsided affair.

This commanding win keeps Chile firmly entrenched at the top of Pool A, boasting a perfect record of 10 points and a massive +105 point differential across their first two matches. The bonus-point victory showcases the rapid developmental growth of Chilean rugby on the global stage. Meanwhile, Romania struggles to find its footing in the competition, facing a steep uphill battle to recover from the tactical and physical showcase put on by the hosts.

In the other Pool A fixture played earlier today, regional rivals Brazil kept their own tournament hopes alive by defeating Hong Kong with a hard-fought 22–10 scoreline. This result sets up a highly anticipated South American clash in the final round of pool play. Brazil will need another strong performance if they hope to disrupt Chile’s dominant momentum, while Hong Kong and Romania will look to play spoilers and salvage pride in their respective final group games.

The tournament schedule now shifts toward the decisive final round of group phase matches, which will determine who advances to the knockout stages. Chile will look to secure the absolute top spot in Pool A when they square off against a confident Brazil side on Monday, October 12, at 7pm local time. Fans expecting a fierce regional derby will be watching closely to see if Chile can maintain their flawless run or if Brazil can pull off a noteworthy upset.
